rows.episode_title: Wolfboy Finds Adventure
rows.synopsis: Wolfboy spies curious-looking creatures at his new boarding school and follows them down a glowing portal.
rows.situation: Wolfboy arrives at a new boarding school already braced for rejection: the other kids mocked his mask and called him weird, and his mum named the thing out loud. He wears the mask anyway because it is the only self he has liked so far.
rows.coping: He follows the strange creatures instead of unpacking, hides what he is to stay, and when a storm cloud creature melts down he names his own inside spaghetti and fireworks and offers it a hug. The hug works, the professor lets him stay, and the mask stays on by choice.
rows.notes: mixed age: the hug-a-cloud resolution plays 2-4; being the weird kid at a new school and finding your people, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'spies curious-looking creatures and follows them down a glowing portal' omits the bullying backstory, the mum conversation, and the emotional labor of the Floof rescue. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The weird kid with the wolf mask follows two strangers down a portal rather than face another school where he does not fit. When their pet cloud has the meltdown he knows from the inside, Wolfboy talks it down with a hug, and the realm of sprytes decides the oddballs are exactly who changes the world. He stays, mask on, belonging for the first time.

rows.episode_title: Wolfboy Gets a Bed / Wolfboy Makes a Blunder
rows.synopsis: Sprytes from the rival dorm challenge Wolfboy to complete the risky star trial. Wolfboy creates a peculiar little friend.
rows.situation: The rival dorm demands the first-night Star Trial, and refusing means standing out as even more of an outsider than a human pretending to be a spryte already is. The Star Creature hates surface dwellers and Wolfboy cannot float.
rows.coping: He goes anyway, admits the true reason, that a star means he does not have to go home, and the Great Wolf gives him a scale without a trick. Whatever happened at the lake stays a mystery, but he has a bunk and friends who decorated it.
rows.notes: older: high-stakes trial, disguised identity, and a stranger reading the truth, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'challenge Wolfboy to complete the risky star trial' omits the Stargazer confrontation and the honesty payoff. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: New kid Wolfboy accepts the rival dorm's Star Trial on his first night rather than be the spryte who refused. At the tower the fearsome Star Creature sees through his disguise, and he wins a star by telling the truth: he just wants to stay. His friends have already made him a bunk.

rows.episode_title: Wolfboy Gets a Bed / Wolfboy Makes a Blunder
rows.synopsis: Sprytes from the rival dorm challenge Wolfboy to complete the risky star trial. Wolfboy creates a peculiar little friend.
rows.situation: In clay class, Wolfboy improvises wings and horns on a rabbit the handbook says must be exact, and Xandra names the result a blunder. Hopton bolts through the factory endangering everyone, headed for a portal to the surface.
rows.coping: The Blunder Dungeon reframes the mistake: a griffin, a wyvern, a jackalope, incredible creatures nobody was supposed to want. Hopton was not rampaging, she needed room to let off steam, and she finds her home with the gamekeeper.
rows.notes: mixed age: the explodeling rabbit chaos plays 2-4; creative work that breaks the rules being called a mistake, and blunders as a home for misfits, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Wolfboy creates a peculiar little friend' omits the handbook conflict, the rampaging sequence, and the Blunder Dungeon reframe. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Wolfboy's winged explodeling rabbit violates the sacred Spryte Handbook and escapes through the factory, and Xandra calls it what everyone calls wrong creations: a blunder. The Blunder Dungeon shows him a dungeon full of glorious creatures nobody meant to make, and Hopton finds her people. Blunders can be pretty cool.

rows.episode_title: There's Trouble in the Wood / Sprout Makes the Team
rows.synopsis: Wolfboy, Xandra, and Sprout volunteer to care for sick trees. A spryte game between dorms brings out Xandra's competitive side.
rows.situation: Flora's wood is fogged and its trees are dying, and the fog hides the cause well enough that no one can fight it. The class stories have also made Sprout terrified that disarrays are everywhere, and getting lost in the fog separates him from the group.
rows.coping: The mystery unpacks in two layers: rotter slugs are the real tree-killers and the fog is their cover, so Wolfboy rebuilds a human contraption with tape and imagination to clear it. The dead tree becomes soil, and Sprout plants it forward.
rows.notes: mixed age: the slug-and-fog mystery plays 2-4; named villains being a cover for a smaller boring problem, and a loss composted into new growth, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'volunteer to care for sick trees' omits the fog cover, the contraption rebuild, and the tree funeral. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Flora's wood is fogged and sick, and the fog turns out to be cover for rotter slugs doing the real damage. Wolfboy rebuilds a human contraption to blow the fog away, the slugs scatter once visible, and one lost tree is buried into the dirt so something new can grow there.

rows.episode_title: There's Trouble in the Wood / Sprout Makes the Team
rows.synopsis: Wolfboy, Xandra, and Sprout volunteer to care for sick trees. A spryte game between dorms brings out Xandra's competitive side.
rows.situation: Sprout is the only Figwort left out of Guardians and Disarrays because his dorm cannot field a team, and Xandra knows exactly why joining is risky: they will lose, in public, badly.
rows.coping: Xandra plays anyway for Sprout's sake, hates it, then finds the actual point: they are the worst team and having the most fun. Losing a million games with Sprout beats one point with Tali, and Sprout scores the winning run to a one-sided cheer.
rows.notes: mixed age: the playground game plays 2-4; loyalty versus winning, and choosing the team that lets everyone play, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'brings out Xandra's competitive side' omits Sprout's exclusion, her losing-with-love turnaround, and the win. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Sprout cannot field a Guardians and Disarrays team, so Xandra risks her pride to play on the worst roster in the game. The team loses gloriously and wins anyway, and Xandra's verdict outlasts the score: rather lose a million games with Sprout than win one with the rival dorm.

rows.episode_title: Losing Track of Time / Chaos Comes to Class
rows.synopsis: The gang goes on a time-traveling adventure to undo Wolfboy's mistake. A disarray attack unleashes something really powerful.
rows.situation: Wolfboy breaks Sprout's grandfather's twig of enduring friendship, the promise attached to it breaks too, and the apology does not fix the object. The forbidden stairs to the past look like the one undo button.
rows.coping: The trip confirms Chronopher's rule the hard way: touching the past unravels other things, and the stick cannot come home. Sprout breaks the fix-it loop instead, splitting the broken twig into three keepsakes, one for each friend.
rows.notes: older: regret, tampering with the past, and accepting that broken means broken, land 5-7; the keepsake sharing plays younger. script_vs_synopsis: 'time-traveling adventure to undo Wolfboy's mistake' omits the friendship-token stakes, the near-paradoxes, and the three-ways split resolution. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Wolfboy breaks the heirloom twig that sealed his friendship with Sprout, and a stairwell trip to the past teaches the class rule by near-disaster: you cannot unbreak things. Sprout splits the two halves three ways instead, one piece per friend, and the friendship survives its own souvenir.

rows.episode_title: Losing Track of Time / Chaos Comes to Class
rows.synopsis: The gang goes on a time-traveling adventure to undo Wolfboy's mistake. A disarray attack unleashes something really powerful.
rows.situation: Guardian Lab's shape-shifting scurillion drills turn real when disarrays infiltrate the training, and friend and foe become indistinguishable on purpose. Wolfboy is the target, and his taped-together gear is dismissed as toys.
rows.coping: Wolfboy learns to read the difference between friends and copies, and Excaliboom, the homemade light lance everyone mocked, is the thing that ends the attack with a boom. The toys were the preparation all along.
rows.notes: older: shape-shifting enemies and trust under pressure land 5-7; the homemade-gadget payoff plays all ages. script_vs_synopsis: 'a disarray attack unleashes something really powerful' omits the scurillion confusion game and the Excaliboom vindication. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Guardian Lab's shape-shifter training goes live when disarrays impersonate Xandra, Athena, and friends, and Wolfboy must tell true friends from copies while his homemade gear earns its laughs. Excaliboom's boom ends the attack, and the kid who showed up with toys turns out to be the one who was prepared.

rows.episode_title: Wolfboy Finds a Memory
rows.synopsis: Wolfboy, Xandra, and Sprout sneak into the Memory Maze to find out why Luxcraft’s pendant is so familiar to Wolfboy.
rows.situation: Luxcraft grounds the trio and refuses to say who Wolfboy really is, and the hazy pendant memory is the only thread. Sneaking into a forbidden maze to find your own memories, guarded by memory mites that eat them, is the risk Xandra named a grumpy bum over.
rows.coping: Wolfboy's memory book yields the pendant sighting and a recording of Luxcraft arguing to bring him to the Factory for a destiny someone else is coming for. Xandra's own backstory surfaces, her guardian parents died young, and the three leave the maze closer than they entered it, while the queen's side learns the boy is here.
rows.notes: older: identity mystery, lost parents in a friend's past, and a villain learning where the hero is, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'why Luxcraft's pendant is so familiar' omits the memory mites, the Xandra orphan reveal, and the prophecy argument. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Grounded and stonewalled by Luxcraft, Wolfboy sneaks into the Memory Maze to find his own memory of the professor's pendant, with Sprout and a grudging Xandra. The maze answers more than asked: Luxcraft fought to protect a destiny the queen is already hunting, Xandra lost her guardian parents young, and the three friends come out trusting each other with their whole stories.

rows.episode_title: Wolfboy Goes Home / Wolfboy Makes a Snowflake
rows.synopsis: Xandra and Sprout join Wolfboy on his trip home to see his mother. Wolfboy helps Blip find his confidence.
rows.situation: Wolfboy goes home with a cracked mask and a head full of questions, and every direct one to his mum gets deflected by his own second secret: she thinks he is at a normal school. The attic holds a second wolf mask, younger photos, and a song she used to play him, and still no answer about who he is.
rows.coping: Mum gives him the truest thing she has: nobody can tell you who you are, you figure it out for yourself and listen to your heart. The sprytes' clue hunt turns up a photo that suggests his story is older than either of them has said, and they leave carrying it together.
rows.notes: older: identity questions held open, a parent keeping and receiving secrets, and clues in an attic, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'trip home to see his mother' omits the double secret, the mask mending, and the photo clue. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Wolfboy brings his spryte friends home to mend Mum-made mask and ask Mum-made questions, all while she believes he is at a human school. The attic yields a twin mask and a photo that deepens the mystery instead of closing it, and his mum hands over the episode's real answer: nobody can tell you who you are, figure it out and listen to your heart.

rows.episode_title: Wolfboy Goes Home / Wolfboy Makes a Snowflake
rows.synopsis: Xandra and Sprout join Wolfboy on his trip home to see his mother. Wolfboy helps Blip find his confidence.
rows.situation: Blip is a perfectionist about everything except the two things Snow Lab demands: making a unique snowflake and then dancing with it in public. His all-night practicing is already failing before the humiliation part arrives.
rows.coping: Wolfboy hands Blip an ordinary balloon dressed as a dance orb from a rhythm spryte, and the confidence it lends works: Blip dances beautifully. When the reveal comes, the lesson is his to keep, he just had to believe he could do it.
rows.notes: mixed age: the balloon gag plays 2-4; performance anxiety and borrowed confidence becoming real confidence, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Wolfboy helps Blip find his confidence' omits the placebo mechanism and the honest reveal. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Blip can make a perfect snowflake but cannot dance with it in front of anyone, and practice is making him worse. Wolfboy's fake dance orb, actually just a balloon, gives him the belief the night of the performance, and the honest reveal lands gently: the power was Blip's, the orb was a nudge. Snow falls like celebration.

rows.episode_title: Grandmother Tells a Story / Grandmother Loses Her Crown
rows.synopsis: Wolfboy visits Xandra and Sprout's home to celebrate Elderspryte Day. Grandmother Figwort's beloved crown is stolen by a bogmarsh beast.
rows.situation: Elderspryte Day at Figwort Farm is a house of caution for a kid whose parents died as heroes: twenty-four siblings, mottoes about running away and curling into a ball, and a family story that ends with the betrayal that lost Xandra her parents. Everyone works hard not to mention them.
rows.coping: Sprout's story fills the gap: Xandra's parents ambushed by scrawmongers and never afraid, told out loud by the kid who never talks about it. The family motto world gets its counterweight, and Xandra lets Wolfboy hold the part of her story nobody says.
rows.notes: older: grieving parents, a family story that names the loss, land 5-7; the farm warmth plays all ages. script_vs_synopsis: 'celebrate Elderspryte Day' omits the motto-of-caution culture, the Great Betrayal story, and Xandra's private story about her parents. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Wolfboy spends Elderspryte Day inside the Figworts' loving safety culture, where the mottoes all run away from danger, and learns the reason for Xandra's guardedness: the Great Betrayal story names the day her parents were lost. Her private story about their fearlessness gives the family's caution something to measure up to.

rows.episode_title: Grandmother Tells a Story / Grandmother Loses Her Crown
rows.synopsis: Wolfboy visits Xandra and Sprout's home to celebrate Elderspryte Day. Grandmother Figwort's beloved crown is stolen by a bogmarsh beast.
rows.situation: The bogmarsh beast makes off with Grandmother Figwort's crown, her late husband's one reckless masterpiece of off-path love, and Sprout's whole training is to run away and curl into a ball.
rows.coping: Wolfboy and Xandra lure Sprout off the path to gather new crown flowers, and when the beast returns Sprout stands his ground, scared and offering flowers anyway. His family discovers bravery was a Figwort trait all along, Grandfather Cypress's kind, and the crown is replaced and re-crowned.
rows.notes: mixed age: the beast chase plays 2-4; being scared and doing the thing anyway as a working definition of brave, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'crown is stolen by a bogmarsh beast' omits the off-path theme, Grandfather Cypress's story, and Sprout's flower offering. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The bogmarsh beast steals Grandmother's crown, woven by a late husband who broke every path rule for love, and homebody Sprout must decide which family tradition is his. Off the path, with friends who came to help him be brave, he faces the beast with flowers instead of flight. The new crown earns a hero's badge and a very muddy hug.

rows.episode_title: Nobody Started It! / Wolfboy Begins His Training
rows.synopsis: Dorm rivalry reaches peak silliness with an all-out prank war. Luxcraft begins training Wolfboy to harness his powers.
rows.situation: The dorm is wrecked, Tali's look convinces everyone who did it, and the retaliation escalates past everyone's intent: glitter dolphins, gravity eggs, water orbs, lights-out citations. Nobody checks the evidence before the first prank flies.
rows.coping: Floof runs the actual investigation: wilted leaves, a rusty spoon, teeth marks, and a disarray identification. The prank war ends with mutual apologies, and the real intruders were after something, or someone.
rows.notes: mixed age: the prank escalation plays 2-4; blame assigned before evidence, and an apology when it was wrong, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'all-out prank war' omits the false accusation of Tali and Floof's disarray forensics. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: A trashed dorm room launches a prank war on the rival dorm, built entirely on a look Wolfboy swears was evidence. Floof's actual investigation clears Tali and names the culprit: disarrays, hunting in the dorm for someone. The pranks end in apologies and the mystery gets much bigger.

rows.episode_title: Nobody Started It! / Wolfboy Begins His Training
rows.synopsis: Dorm rivalry reaches peak silliness with an all-out prank war. Luxcraft begins training Wolfboy to harness his powers.
rows.situation: Luxcraft confirms the prophecy out loud, a human child who restores balance at a time of great darkness, then locks Wolfboy's questions behind a training contract and a warning: confiding in friends endangers them. Wolfboy's first lie to Xandra and Sprout is already in his mouth.
rows.coping: The wisps get the collaboration not the command: listen, drop the guard, let them see who you really are. The parrot flies, the prophecy is confirmed, and Wolfboy heads back with the secret that will strain his first real friendships.
rows.notes: older: prophecy, secrets kept for other people's safety, and a first lie by omission, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Luxcraft begins training Wolfboy' omits the prophecy confirmation and the warning that drives his secrecy. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Luxcraft takes Wolfboy to the heart of the Factory to train his wisp-collaboration, and the wisps respond to being seen, not commanded. The prophecy about the human child is confirmed on the record, along with the instruction that keeps it secret even from Sprout and Xandra. Training begins with wonder and a small, growing silence.

rows.episode_title: We Laugh and Cry / We Don't Know Who to Trust
rows.synopsis: Wolfboy's secret training leaves him no time to focus on the Laugh Lab assignment. Wolfboy tells his friends the truth about the prophecy.
rows.situation: Wolfboy is skipping Sprout's play rehearsals for secret world-saving training, telling himself one matters more, and the missed performance ends in detention and a broken stem promise. The apology that would fix it is the one secret he is forbidden to tell.
rows.coping: Wolfboy chooses the friendship over the secrecy and tells the truth: the prophecy, the powers, the wisp cavern, and the danger rule. The friends do not believe him yet, but the breach is honest, and the pipes trip to prove it begins.
rows.notes: older: a broken promise to a friend, the cost of a noble secret, land 5-7; the Laugh Lab play plays all ages. script_vs_synopsis: 'no time to focus on the Laugh Lab assignment' omits the missed show, the detention, and the full confession. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Secret hero training eats every rehearsal for Sprout's Laugh Lab play, and Wolfboy misses the performance itself, detention included. Choosing honesty over the safety rule, he tells his friends about the prophecy and the powers, and they do not believe a word of it, which is its own kind of hurt. The proof trip starts in the pipes.

rows.episode_title: We Laugh and Cry / We Don't Know Who to Trust
rows.segment_title: We Don't Know Who to Trust
rows.synopsis: Wolfboy's secret training leaves him no time to focus on the Laugh Lab assignment. Wolfboy tells his friends the truth about the prophecy.
rows.situation: The proof expedition through the pipes keeps failing: the Whithervane misleads, Xandra's patience is gone, and a pipe-dweller who lives by never trusting anyone wants the friends to stay broken apart.
rows.coping: The pipe-dweller's birthday-party story shows where distrust leads, living alone in a pipe, and the group chooses each other instead. They reach the wisp cavern in time to overhear the adults deciding what Wolfboy may be allowed to know.
rows.notes: older: trusting a friend who broke a promise, and what never trusting anyone costs, land 5-7; the pipe adventure plays all ages. script_vs_synopsis: 'Wolfboy tells his friends the truth' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Wolfboy leads his doubting friends through the factory pipes to prove the wisp cavern exists, and the journey keeps nearly breaking them, misleading Whithervane and a lonely pipe-dweller teaching distrust. Overhearing Luxcraft and the memory guardians arguing over what Wolfboy should be allowed to know vindicates him: the secret was real, and so was the danger.

rows.episode_title: Wolfboy Follows His Dreams
rows.synopsis: An intense dream causes Wolfboy to sleepwalk toward a forbidden area, so the gang heads to the Dream Lab for help.
rows.situation: The dream voice promising answers about who Wolfboy really is pulls him sleepwalking toward the forbidden passage, and waking him does nothing. The one entity offering the truth is also the one everyone, including Luxcraft, has barred the door against.
rows.coping: The Dream Lab expedition, raised-by-dreams Oneira and Captain Springhaart, ends at the boundary where the voice wears a face: Nyx, who denies the betrayal story and claims to know what he is truly capable of. Wolfboy declines the new dream, because his dreams might know him better than anyone.
rows.notes: older: sleepwalking, a manipulative stranger in dreams, and refusing a quick fix to keep your own dreams, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'heads to the Dream Lab for help' omits the Nyx contact, the boundary-crossing, and Wolfboy's choice to keep the dream. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: A voice in Wolfboy's dreams walks him toward the forbidden passage until his friends chase the sleepwalk through River Lab, then the Dream Lab supplies a new-dream solution and an expedition to the Dreamscape boundary instead. There the voice gains a name, Nyx, who claims the adults are the liars. Wolfboy turns down the replacement dream and keeps his own.

rows.episode_title: Wolfboy Takes a Ride / Wolfboy Talks with Nyx
rows.synopsis: Wolfboy steps through the infamous "passage" and finds himself in the Disarray Realm. Wolfboy finally meets Nyx.
rows.situation: The passage is finally open and Wolfboy walks into the realm everyone fears, alone, on the promise of answers. The spryte side is running a cover story about a sick friend, and Nyx's realm is a wasteland with a two-day wait and generals who do not want him there.
rows.coping: He spends the wait finding a stolen wheel for the disarrays and discovering they are hungry, not evil, which becomes the episode's thesis in one act of seeing them clearly. He reaches Nyx and hears the first version of the truth: the world runs on a cycle of creation and destruction, and both halves matter.
rows.notes: older: crossing into the enemy's world and questioning everything the adults said, land 5-7; the wheel chase plays younger. script_vs_synopsis: 'steps through the passage and finds the Disarray Realm' omits the humanitis cover story, the stolen wheel, and the balance-of-nature reveal. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Wolfboy crosses the forbidden passage into the Disarray Realm while his friends stall Luxcraft with a fake case of humanitis. Helping hungry disarrays recover their stolen wheel reframes the enemy, and Nyx's court opens the season's argument: creation and destruction are a cycle, and Wolfboy may be needed by the other side.

rows.episode_title: Wolfboy Takes a Ride / Wolfboy Talks with Nyx
rows.synopsis: Wolfboy steps through the infamous "passage" and finds himself in the Disarray Realm. Wolfboy finally meets Nyx.
rows.situation: Nyx tells Wolfboy that the spryte side suppresses destruction, that the twin trees Dryades and Meliae measure the imbalance, and that the prophecy means the disarrays need him. She offers destruction-wisp training and one night to decide.
rows.coping: The episode leaves him mid-persuasion with a disturbingly coherent argument and a court of disarray generals watching. The spryte narrative of good versus evil is complicated for good.
rows.notes: older: moral symmetry, propaganda on both sides, and a mentor with motives, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'finally meets Nyx' omits the Dryades and Meliae balance mechanics and the destruction-wisp offer. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Nyx makes her case: disarrays do necessary work, the twin trees track the world's imbalance, and the prophecy means the disarrays need Wolfboy's help to rise. Destruction-wisp training is on offer, the generals grumble, and the season's central question lands: what if the enemy's story about the world is partly true?

rows.episode_title: Nyx Answers a Question / Wolfboy and Seth Escape
rows.synopsis: While honing his destruction powers, Wolfboy meets a young disarray named Seth. Startling discoveries are made.
rows.situation: Destruction-wisp training is fun, and Nyx's answer about Xandra's parents, accidents happen during war, is neither a confession nor a comfort. Meanwhile Serebrin and the generals have decided a human in the court is a threat, and Seth the drawing disarray is already spying on him.
rows.coping: Seth's hideout friendship says what the adults will not: Nyx charms and disarrays fall for it, and the generals are coming tonight. Wolfboy learns his own dual power, creation and destruction wisps, is the thing both courts want, and nobody in power is telling him the whole truth.
rows.notes: older: war casualties described as accidents, secret plotting, land 5-7; the drawing friendship plays all ages. script_vs_synopsis: 'meets a young disarray named Seth' omits the parents-accident answer, the general conspiracy, and the dual-wisp reveal. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Training destruction wisps with Nyx, Wolfboy hears her non-answer about Xandra's parents and befriends Seth, a disarray who draws spryte things and trusts nobody in the court. The generals plot to remove the human, and Wolfboy learns he is the only being who can wield both kinds of wisp. Everyone with power wants to be the one holding it.

rows.episode_title: Nyx Answers a Question / Wolfboy and Seth Escape
rows.synopsis: While honing his destruction powers, Wolfboy meets a young disarray named Seth. Startling discoveries are made.
rows.situation: Escape night: Seth risks exile to guide Wolfboy through the Dreamscape, the generals hunt in every crater, and Seth's fear is leaving the only realm she knows for a world that may reject a disarray. The rescue crew of sprytes is improvising badly on the other side.
rows.coping: The escape works by making: Wolfboy sculpts a destruction-wisp tub-portal that carries them home, and the rescue squad stumbles in right on time. Seth crosses the border into the spryte realm on the episode's thesis: friends are what make a place feel like home.
rows.notes: mixed age: the tub-portal chase plays 2-4; taking a friend into a world that may not accept them, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Wolfboy and Seth escape' omits the Dreamscape route, the rescue squad plan, and Seth's fit-in fear. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Seth guides Wolfboy home ahead of the generals' midnight sweep, trading her safety for his, and his answer to her fear of not fitting in is the episode's moral: friends make a place a home. A sculpted portal, a chaotic rescue squad, and one disarray refugee later, the spryte realm gains a new roommate.

rows.episode_title: A Dinosaur Comes for Tea / Things Seem Unsound
rows.synopsis: Xandra and Sprout have a difficult time warming up to Seth. The value of Seth's skills come to light after a d
rows.situation: Seth is home, technically, but Xandra wants her gone and will not leave her alone with the dorm, while Seth concludes she is a walking disaster whose only future is hiding where no one is. A forbidden Dinosaur Lab visit gives her destruction power its best day: a real dinosaur as a thank-you.
rows.coping: The dinosaur chaos proves the point in the wrong direction at first, then Wolfboy reframes: she melted the ice into a slide, made a mini Norman, saved the day. Xandra allows the houseguest, conditionally, and Sprout's mask gift makes her one of the household.
rows.notes: mixed age: the dinosaur caper plays 2-4; a skeptic learning to give a newcomer a chance after she has already earned it, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'difficult time warming up to Seth' omits the Dinosaur Lab adventure, Norman Jr, and Xandra's conditional acceptance. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Seth the disarray moves into the dorm over Xandra's objections, and her thank-you gift, a real dinosaur from the forbidden Dinosaur Lab, causes exactly the chaos Xandra predicted. But the chaos includes a slide made from melted ice and a sculpture that saves the day, and the house reluctantly grows by one. A miniature Norman seals the friendship.

rows.episode_title: A Dinosaur Comes for Tea / Things Seem Unsound
rows.synopsis: Xandra and Sprout have a difficult time warming up to Seth. The value of Seth's skills come to light after a d
rows.situation: A disguised Seth's first Sound Lab goes wrong in front of everyone, and when every sound in the factory starts switching places, the room assigns blame to the disarray in the doorway. Her innocence is hard to prove with a track record.
rows.coping: Seth identifies the culprit as a Muddler, harmless mischief in its nature, and finds the real solution: the one sound that holds its attention is a nightingale, because the Disarray Realm never gets to hear anything lovely. Knowledge of both worlds is the tool, and the classroom learns to stop guessing.
rows.notes: mixed age: the sound-switching chaos plays 2-4; being blamed because of who you are, and redeeming yourself with insider knowledge nobody else has, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'value of Seth's skills come to light' omits the Muddler chase and the nightingale insight. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Seth's first class in a spryte disguise collides with a sound-scrambling Muddler, and the blame lands on the known disarray before the facts do. Seth names the creature, explains its nature, and ends the crisis with a nightingale song, the beautiful thing her realm never hears. Being from both worlds turns out to be the useful one.

rows.episode_title: The Color Fades / Wolfboy Frolics with the Enemy
rows.synopsis: Vibrant flowers on the surface come under attack from the disarrays. Xandra's favorite comic series reveals cl
rows.situation: Color Lab is canceled because Professor Pigment has lost her spark: fading and repainting the same valley forever feels pointless, and the disarrays have never been this coordinated. The creative engine of the spryte side is quietly burning out.
rows.coping: Wolfboy reframes fading as a blank slate and builds Seth a portal so no one is left behind, and her rule-breaking color chaos in the drained valley is the most inspiring thing Pigment has seen in years. Creative block turns out to be input starvation, and the cure was a fresh eye.
rows.notes: older: burnout, the meaning of repeating creative work, land 5-7; the repainting plays younger. script_vs_synopsis: 'vibrant flowers under attack' omits Pigment's creative block, the bespoke portal, and Seth's chaos-as-inspiration. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The disarrays drain a whole valley faster than the color sprytes can repaint it, and Professor Pigment has stopped painting because she cannot see the point. Wolfboy's reframe, every fade is a blank slate, plus Seth's chaotic outside-the-lines colors, hands the professor her spark back. The valley ends more beautiful than the blueprint.

rows.episode_title: The Color Fades / Wolfboy Frolics with the Enemy
rows.synopsis: Vibrant flowers on the surface come under attack from the disarrays. Xandra's favorite comic series reveals cl
rows.situation: The prophecy hunt hits its wall: no legend mentions a human, and Xandra pushes Wolfboy toward answers he is increasingly avoiding. Playing hooky with Tali in Gem Lab feels better than destiny, and the reason comes out finally.
rows.coping: Wolfboy names it himself: everything rides on him and he is scared of failing, of not being what everyone thinks. Xandra stops pushing and promises to be there when he is ready, and the Lost Volume's Astralynx symbol, matching Luxcraft's pendant, keeps the mystery open for braver days.
rows.notes: older: fear of failing a destiny, avoidance as a feeling not a flaw, land 5-7; the Gem Lab ride plays younger. script_vs_synopsis: 'favorite comic series reveals cl...' omits the Lost Volume, the Legends Society, and the scared admission. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Xandra's comic research and a secret Legends Society yield the Lost Volume and a pendant-matching symbol, while Wolfboy dodges training for joyrides with the rival dorm. The confrontation he was avoiding becomes the episode's gift: he says he is scared, and Xandra chooses patience over prophecy.

rows.episode_title: The Bubble Is Popped / Xandra Finds a Memory
rows.synopsis: The sprytes celebrate their most beloved holiday: Bubble Day! Xandra finds the strength to watch the one memor
rows.situation: Bubble Day's whispering ceremony asks everyone to name fears into a bubble and let them go, and Wolfboy's bubble holds the big ones: not a hero, letting everyone down. Seth is excluded by a broken bubble and a broken welcome, and then scurillions shatter the ceremony and every whispered fear escapes into the crowd.
rows.coping: The attack gives the fears shape but not power: the sprytes defend, Seth is sent to safety, and the day's lesson holds, naming a fear was never the same as living it. Nyx uses the chaos to destroy two spryte portals with a device Wolfboy's training helped create.
rows.notes: mixed age: the bubble games and fear-naming play 2-4; the ceremony hijack and portal destruction land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'celebrate their most beloved holiday' omits the whisper ritual, the escaped fears, and Nyx's portal weapon. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Bubble Day's ceremony invites the whole factory to whisper fears into bubbles and float them away, and Wolfboy's are the heaviest: not special enough, letting everyone down. A scurillion attack pops the ceremony open, every fear escapes into a frightened crowd, and Nyx marks the day by destroying two spryte portals with a weapon Wolfboy inadvertently inspired.

rows.episode_title: The Bubble Is Popped / Xandra Finds a Memory
rows.synopsis: The sprytes celebrate their most beloved holiday: Bubble Day! Xandra finds the strength to watch the one memor
rows.situation: Luxcraft's council presentation collapses into accusation, and Xandra forces the truth she has dodged all her life: her father's last memory, watched, not retold. The memory shows her parents defeated, Luxcraft stopping an annihilation of the disarrays alongside Nyx, and a story she inherited as simple betrayal becoming anything but.
rows.coping: The episode honors the hardest feeling on the board: the grown-up you trusted knew the truth about your parents and never told you. Xandra's trust in Luxcraft breaks exactly as Wolfboy's did, and the two of them face the same question from opposite sides.
rows.notes: older: watching a parent's final memory, discovering adults' compartmentalized truths, land 5-7; nothing here plays young. script_vs_synopsis: 'finds the strength to watch the one memor[y]' omits the amalgam-orb reveal, Luxcraft's stand with Nyx, and Xandra's rupture. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Xandra chooses the memory she has avoided her whole life: her father's last, which shows the battle lost and Luxcraft refusing to wipe out the disarrays, standing with Nyx to stop it. The betrayal story that named her parents' killer becomes a moral fog, and her trust in Luxcraft breaks beside Wolfboy's. Both kids now hold the same unfinished question.

rows.episode_title: Wolfboy Takes the Plunge / The Stars Are Restored
rows.synopsis: Luxcraft's decision leaves Wolfboy feeling even more unsure about who to trust. The gang makes a shocking disc
rows.situation: The council orders Wolfboy confined to the dorm while the portal war worsens, the elders want to deploy him as a weapon, and Nyx's Nosehound hauls him toward a destiny he did not choose. Everyone has a plan for him, and he has agreed to none of them.
rows.coping: Wolfboy refuses to be deployed by either court and tells his friends they are going to find the prophecy themselves. Taking the plunge means choosing his own question over everyone's answers.
rows.notes: older: being conscripted by both sides, agency over destiny, land 5-7; the Coral Lab sequence plays younger. script_vs_synopsis: 'unsure about who to trust' omits the dorm confinement, the Nosehound capture, and the decision to self-direct the quest. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The council confines Wolfboy as a prophecy weapon, Nyx's Nosehound drags him toward the opposite destiny, and neither asked him. Escaping into Coral Lab with his friends, he declines both scripts and sets out to find the prophecy himself. Nobody gets to be the hero of his story but him.

rows.episode_title: Wolfboy Takes the Plunge / The Stars Are Restored
rows.synopsis: Luxcraft's decision leaves Wolfboy feeling even more unsure about who to trust. The gang makes a shocking disc
rows.situation: The Star Creature knows Astralynx and will not help, because sprytelings have been stealing its stars for centuries as a hazing tradition. Asking again means fixing the theft first.
rows.coping: The gang returns every star they can find and makes a handmade singing star to cover the rest, and the gesture earns the map: the symbol marks four Ancients, Sky, Mountain, Water, Forest, whose wisdom the quest must now seek. Apology first, answers after.
rows.notes: mixed age: the star-crafting plays 2-4; repairing a harm your community caused before asking for help, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'shocking discovery' omits the star-theft reckoning, the singing star, and the Ancients map. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The Star Creature turns the gang away for a reason no one had named: the Star Trial is theft. Restitution, returned stars plus one handmade singing star, buys more than a plea would, and the creature reveals the symbol as a map to the four Ancients of the Factory. The real quest starts with a thank-you.

rows.episode_title: We Search Above / We Search Below
rows.synopsis: The gang sets off on a quest, but Sprout stays behind to help a critter in need. Seth realizes her true potent
rows.situation: The Sky Ancient turns out to be an angry flock that yells at anyone who tries, because spryteling traditions have wronged it for centuries. Sprout is benched by his own story: everyone on this quest has a destiny except him.
rows.coping: Sprout mends the fallen glider with one feather short, and the Sky Ancient, all of them at once, names his worth: every feather matters, and only together do they soar. His kindness reopens the flock, and the first prophecy line is earned, hope inside a young outsider's mind.
rows.notes: mixed age: the feather-mending plays 2-4; feeling like the extra one on a quest for other people's destinies, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Sprout stays behind to help a critter in need' omits the multi-voiced Ancient, the star theft reckoning's echo, and the first prophecy line. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The Sky Ancient is many voices at once and wants nothing to do with the gang until Sprout, who feels like the least important one on the quest, mends its broken glider feather by feather. The flock's answer doubles as his: every feather has a role, and only together do they soar. First prophecy line secured, and it is about him too.

rows.episode_title: We Search Above / We Search Below
rows.synopsis: The gang sets off on a quest, but Sprout stays behind to help a critter in need. Seth realizes her true potent
rows.situation: The Mountain Ancient is a monster by reputation, red eyes and a roar, and Seth arrives believing her own story: she will always be the disarray who wrecks things. The cave mirrors both fears back at them.
rows.coping: Seth's try-a-ladder improvisation saves the group, and the Mountain Ancient turns out to be a gentle creature who hid because everyone decided what it was. Wolfboy's line lands for both of them: just because someone called you a monster does not make you one. Seth retires the mask.
rows.notes: mixed age: the shadow-monster reveal plays 2-4; self-fulfilling labels and choosing not to hide, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Seth realizes her true potential' omits the monster-not-monster reveal and the retired mask. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The Mountain Ancient everyone fears is hiding for the same reason Seth is: the story others tell about them. Her rock-ladder rescue and Wolfboy's monster-defying handshake bring both of them out of the dark, and the second wisdom line, seeing what could be, is received by a group that no longer needs the monster costume. Seth leaves her mask behind.

rows.episode_title: We Search for Balance / We Search for Change
rows.synopsis: Wolfboy and the gang must help the Water Ancients resolve an old feud. In the Forest Zone, the gang meets a ve
rows.situation: The Water Zone is dry because the Water Ancient split in two over how to be: the Ice Ancient wants stillness, the Steam Ancient wants motion, and each is certain the other is the problem. The gang gets a full, justified case from each side.
rows.coping: Wolfboy's fake telephone makes each half be the first to reach out, and the mediator's line does the rest: you are both right and both wrong, and you both want to be water again. The reunited Ancient yields the third prophecy piece, each side to the other's bound.
rows.notes: mixed age: the phone gag plays 2-4; a two-sided feud where both sides are right, and moving past who started it, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'resolve an old feud' omits the split-identity mechanism, the fake call, and the both-right resolution. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The dried-up Water Zone holds an Ancient split in two, Ice versus Steam, each with a legitimate case against the other. Wolfboy's human telephone trick gets them talking, balance gets them whole, and the third prophecy line arrives as the water returns. Being right was the cheapest thing on the mountain.

rows.episode_title: We Search for Balance / We Search for Change
rows.synopsis: Wolfboy and the gang must help the Water Ancients resolve an old feud. In the Forest Zone, the gang meets a ve
rows.situation: The Forest Ancient is a caterpillar in a cocoon he built himself, stalling with endless busywork tasks because the winds of change are blowing whether he is ready or not. The gang keeps wrapping him safer instead of asking what is inside.
rows.coping: Seth opens the cocoon, and the frightened Ancient hears the episode's thesis from his own visitors: everything changes, it is part of life, and you must not fear it. He flies, the winds of change blow, and the final wisdom is seeds of change blooming when dreamers fill the world with light.
rows.notes: mixed age: the cocoon reveal plays 2-4; being scared of change you cannot stop, and a helper who waits too long, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'meets a ve[ry strange...]' omits the caterpillar impostor, the task stalling, and the transformation. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The Forest Ancient is a caterpillar hiding in his own cocoon, assigning the gang increasingly absurd tasks to postpone his first flight. Seth's kindness ends the stall: it is okay to be scared, but the winds of change must blow. The last prophecy piece lands as he blooms, and the four pieces of wisdom are complete.

rows.episode_title: Wolfboy's Heart to Heart / The World's in Disarray
rows.synopsis: A frustrated Wolfboy feels overwhelmed by the pressures of being a hero. Newfound clarity guides Wolfboy to me
rows.situation: The completed prophecy is just a poem, every mentor has a different plan for him, and Wolfboy misses his mum enough to wish himself home. A dream-adventure with a small sad adventurer named William shows him the mask was never a hiding place, and Mum's verdict reframes everything: a hero's mask reveals what is underneath.
rows.coping: Newfound clarity: nobody can give the answer, changing the world starts with being your true self, from within. He wakes with a plan of his own for the first time, to talk Nyx down instead of fighting her.
rows.notes: mixed age: the dream quest and the mask talk play 2-4; hero pressure, homesickness, and the reveal-not-hide reframe, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'overwhelmed by the pressures of being a hero' omits the dream encounter, the mum's reveal-not-hide insight, and the self-chosen plan. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Four prophecy pieces add up to a poem with no instructions, and Wolfboy's hero pressure peaks with homesickness. A dream friendship with another William, and Mum's ruling that a hero's mask reveals rather than hides, hand him the answer no Ancient could: be your true self. He chooses diplomacy over destiny and heads for Nyx.

rows.episode_title: Wolfboy's Heart to Heart / The World's in Disarray
rows.synopsis: A frustrated Wolfboy feels overwhelmed by the pressures of being a hero. Newfound clarity guides Wolfboy to me
rows.situation: Nyx's portal to the spryte realm turns negotiation into catastrophe: her true plan is destroying Dryades to cut humans off entirely, and the peace she promised disarrays is conquest. Wolfboy's portal gift made it all possible, and Seth and Xandra are seized as the atrium falls.
rows.coping: Wolfboy refuses to destroy Dryades, the elders' fortress mentality catches Seth in its net anyway, and the realm scatters toward the Mountain Zone with Nyx chanting his name as her weapon. The cost of the sympathetic-mentor arc lands all at once.
rows.notes: older: an ally's hidden endgame, betrayal by someone who was partly right, land 5-7; the siege plays all ages. script_vs_synopsis: 'Newfound clarity guides Wolfboy to me[et Nyx]' omits the Dryades ultimatum, the portal's role, and the seizure of his friends. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Wolfboy comes to Nyx with a peace plan and discovers hers: destroy Dryades, cut humans off, start the world over as a blank canvas. His refusal triggers the invasion his own portal enabled, the elders' defense net catches his friends, and the realm flees to the mountains with Nyx hunting the boy she intends to aim.

rows.episode_title: Something Quite Unexpected Happens
rows.synopsis: Nyx puts Wolfboy in a difficult position, forcing him to choose between his friends and the fate of the world.
rows.situation: Nyx offers to release his friends if he destroys Dryades, the elders accuse him of joining her, and both courts agree on one thing: he is the key. Siding with either means losing someone.
rows.coping: He fakes compliance, then follows the heartbeat to the heart of the factory and destroys both trees to grow one new one: Everyone Portals, usable by sprytes and disarrays alike. The balance is not a side, it is a shared door, and Mum is at the surface end of it.
rows.notes: older: refusing both sides, sacrificing the two trees to build a shared door, land 5-7; the Everyone Portals ending plays all ages. script_vs_synopsis: 'choose between his friends and the fate of the world' omits the fake-out, the heart of the factory, and the Everyone Portals resolution. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Nyx's hostage trade and the elders' accusation leave Wolfboy one move: find the heart of the factory and rebuild from it. Destruction wisps take both old trees, creation wisps grow a new one open to everyone, spryte and disarray, and the prophecy resolves as a door rather than a victory. Wolfboy goes home to tell Mum everything.
